Three sales posts, one pattern

What actually changed in all three

  • 1
    Say who it's for. "If you're over 60 and starting from zero points…"
  • 2
    Put a number in it. A price, a count, a timeframe. "$22,000." "Six years running." "24 inches."
  • 3
    Name the outcome or the cost, plainly. What they get, or what it costs to keep doing it their way.
  • 4
    No wordplay, no jokes that need context. Clever reads as confusing when somebody is scrolling at speed.
  • ✓
    And end with somewhere to go. A link, a freebie, or a comment keyword.
The test

Show the first line to somebody who has never heard of you, with no photo and no context. If they can tell you what the post is about, it works.

Two we wrote and threw out
Too clever"25 years booking other people's dream trips. These two have never left Oregon."
Clear"We've spent 25 years in the travel industry. Here's what we book differently now."
Means nothing to a stranger"Venue #23 we've measured from the chair."
Clear"Angel Stadium in a wheelchair: where to park, which ramps, and where to sit."
Nobody is scrolling Instagram looking for venue 23. They're looking for the place they're going on Saturday.
One rewritten post is a start. Here's the whole rotation.

The five selling post types

1 · Problemget them to admit it
You name the thing they're stuck on, out loud, so they realize they have the problem you fix.
💬 They comment "that's me"
2 · Proofshow it works
You show a real result. A number, a client's trip, a before and after, or your own outcome.
🔗 They click to find out how
3 · Teachinggive one real step
You give away one whole step of your method, completely, so it works on its own.
📩 They join your email list
4 · Offersay what you sell
You say plainly what you sell, who it's for, what it costs, and how somebody starts.
🛒 They buy, or they ask
5 · Youwhy you and not someone else
You give the one fact about your life that makes you the person to buy this from.
👋 They follow and trust you

The three posts we just rewrote were all number 1 or number 3. Here's what a full month looks like for each of you.

The rule underneath all 25 of those posts

Your free content has to be about the same thing as your paid thing

Still true from last call

Give, give, give, then ask

What changes now is what you're giving. The free stuff has to be a piece of the paid stuff.

And the paid thing is

What a free post structurally can't do

All of it in one searchable place, the full method instead of one step, or you doing it for them.

Free: how we pick a restaurant abroad → Paid: we plan and book the whole trip
Free: step one of the housesit application → Paid: the full course, all five steps
Free: one venue reviewed per week → Paid: all of them, searchable by neighborhood

Posting three times a week? Do two teaching posts and rotate the third through problem, proof, offer, and you.

The rule underneath the ratio

Every week, at least one post names the problem, and at least one post names your offer.

And all five need one place to go

A link, a freebie, or a comment keyword in ManyChat. No click means you taught them for free and handed them back to the algorithm.

The freebie from last call is the door. These posts are what walk people to it.

The actual thing · a name, a format, and a price

What you'd actually sell

Jim & Rhonda "The Done-For-You Trip Plan" A custom itinerary document plus every booking made for them $750 / trip
Mairin & Todd "The Housesitting Playbook" 6 short videos plus the application templates they actually send $97
Cielo & Mike "Accessible LA" A searchable web directory of every venue, filtered by neighborhood $8 / month
Doug "First Class After 60" A PDF guide walking through the exact cards and booking route he used $47
Rhonda "The Conversation" A 90-minute guided family session over Zoom, with the workbook $250 / family
Rhoda "Solo at 70" A trip-planning workbook plus a monthly group call for women over 70 $37
Alyssa "Your First Free Flight" A 6-module points course ending with one booked award ticket $147
Daina "Piano in 12 Weeks" Weekly video lessons plus one 1:1 call a month, for adult beginners $79 / month
Rachel "The Family Devotional" 30 printable dinner-table cards plus a short audio for each week $27

Those prices are starting points to argue with, not recommendations. The point is that every one of these has a name, a format, and a number.
